Euljimyeonok opened in 1985 by the second daughter of Pyongyangmyeonok in Uijeongbu.

Closed for redevelopment in 2022
Re-opening in Nakwon-dong in April 2024!!

This is a place where you can truly experience the deep taste of Pyeongyang Naengmyeon.
A place where chewy noodles and clean broth harmonize.
There are sesame seeds, green onions, and red pepper powder on top, and the amount is enormous.

If you drink the clear but cloudy soup first, you feel cool and refreshed at the same time, and you want to keep drinking it.

The cold meat and half of the boiled pork are well-boiled, bringing out the meat's natural taste and making it soft and elastic.
After slurping down a piece of cold noodles and a piece of meat, the bowl became neater before I knew it.

It was a meal that others would envy, with a bowl of plain cold food in a clean building.
All the staff were friendly and the meal was very enjoyable~
Next time, I’ll look forward to bulgogi and cold noodles. 😘

reviews.text:
Please note. My wife and I went to this restaurant after reading the reviews and getting drenched in the December rain. It was about 20 minutes after the store opened, and two young women were already receiving their meal. Before I could even say I would sit down, a man wearing an apron and glasses shouted loudly in Korean, crossed his arms, and motioned for me to leave. I am 64 years old and I have never seen a restaurant owner act like this. While he kept gesturing for me to leave, I pulled out my Papago translator and tried to understand what he was saying. I asked him through a translator, “Do you think you can’t pay?”, but he didn’t answer. Finally he shouted, “No food!” It was hard to believe that something like this could happen so soon after opening. He crossed his arms again and looked threatening. We eventually left there.
I am white American/Canadian and my wife is Asian. I wish there was another way to report this. Of course, I know that a business owner can refuse service to certain customers, but this was the worst experience I've ever had. Fortunately, we enjoyed excellent meals both in Seoul and elsewhere in Busan. I think it would be a good idea to be very careful going into this place. About 60 meters away there is a great Korean restaurant with friendly service:
Brothers Bulgogi Rice Bowl

From the preparation stage, designer Lee Geon-woo provided us with kind and detailed consultation, and he took care of even the details we hadn't thought of, so we were very impressed. We rented it out during lunchtime, and the ribs with croaker pancakes added were full of flavor and sincerity, and the whole family was satisfied. While walking around Bukchon, I was looking for a quiet place to eat alone and stumbled upon this small restaurant. The signboard that said MSG-free, gluten-free, and vegetarian menu caught my eye. I am not a vegetarian, but I wanted to try dishes made directly from nature.

I was asked to sanitize my hands before entering. The inside of the store was a bit messy. There were all kinds of food piled up next to it, but there was no dust or dirt, and instead there were a lot of plants.

The elderly owner spoke English surprisingly well. It's pretty rare. I ordered cold noodles for 15,000 won, and they made it themselves and it took about 15 minutes. The food itself was delicious, but I wish the toppings were a bit more plentiful.

While we were eating, the owner was also eating. When I finished eating, the host smiled and said, “Oh, I just finished eating too.” She asked me where I was from, and when I told her I was from the Philippines, she complimented me on how pretty I was. I was a little embarrassed, but I said thank you.

I've read comments about her being rude, but I've never experienced it myself. Maybe it's just my mood, but considering my age, it's understandable. Overall, it was a good experience and I appreciate the care she puts into her food.

Avoid this place - really terrible experience

Unless you want to have a stressful and unpleasant meal, avoid it. It was clear the moment I walked in that it was going to be a terrible experience.

The inside looked like a restaurant or warehouse. Boxes were stacked precariously everywhere. It felt like I had entered a DHL logistics center rather than a place to eat. Moreover, Korean news was playing loudly on the computer screen, making it impossible to even try to have a conversation.

The food itself was not memorable at all. Nothing special to say, but to be honest there was no chance of me enjoying the food at all due to the terrible atmosphere and service.

And there is also “service”. The woman who seemed to do everything - serving, cooking, managing, and even washing dishes - was really hostile. She seemed to genuinely dislike people, especially tourists, and made no effort to hide her disdain. We actually got yelled at when we visited, which is unacceptable for any business that deals directly with customers. She seemed completely exhausted and resentful of every customer who came through the door.

If you're a vegan, this place is the antithesis of everything you stand for. The overall experience was contrary to any notion of a pleasant, thoughtful, and respectful dining experience.

Protect your money and your mental health. There are countless places in Seoul that offer delicious food and friendly service. But this is not that kind of place.

reviews.text:
A place where you can enjoy the rich taste of seafood at a reasonable price. If you order a table setting, various seafood dishes are served as a course. Simmered octopus and taco wasabi are common flavors that can be eaten anywhere, and different cockles are served depending on the season. The main dishes, grilled abalone and seafood in a ttukbaegi, are great because you can feel the deep flavor of the ingredients rather than the taste of other seasonings. The seafood pot contains a generous amount of seafood, including octopus and clams, making it the best value for money. There are many branches in Seoul, but this branch, located behind Jonggak Station, has a narrow interior and is located between offices, so it is always crowded. Because it is an open kitchen, you can always see the food being prepared neatly, and the service is also friendly. When ordering grilled abalone, it is recommended to order a full or half-table meal rather than a single item. It may be a bit expensive when ordered individually, but if you order it as a table setting, I recommend it because you can taste a variety of seafood dishes for a little extra.
As a restaurant I often visit, I definitely recommend it and intend to revisit it, and I will try all the other dishes on the menu.

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
This is the same house that once lit up the Internet with “videos of customers gossiping behind their backs.”
I made a reservation partly out of curiosity and partly because I thought it must have some potential to have held on for several years without closing down even after the bad news.
In conclusion, the service was ok, but I was very disappointed in the taste and composition that I expected from sushi.

Upon entering, the staff's attitude was quite polite, as if they were aware of the past controversy, but details were still loose.
When asked where Uni was produced, the ambiguous answer was “Probably around Gangwon-do,” and there were many sections in which the order of the course was difficult to understand.
Above all, the shari was too soggy and the seasoning was off, so it did not bring down the perfection of the sushi itself.
The variation in taste was also boring because the same ingredients were served in different forms and served like a ‘dolmakgi’.

The steamed egg custard served as a free course is the Korean style steamed egg custard itself.
It's warm and fluffy, but doesn't have the silkiness characteristic of chawanmushi.
The sea bass sashimi that followed was served with yuzu sauce, and the freshness engulfed the flesh, causing the fish to flake off.

On the other hand, flounder was the most stable on this day.
Light and firm, just like a textbook.
The problem is that I start repeating the same white fish in the order of sea bream, flounder, and flounder (re-appearing), and “white meat again?” A sigh came naturally.

Whelk are an unexpected harvest in the Tsumami section.
It was plump without any fishy smell, and although it was disappointing that the amount of amberjack was small, the balance between oil and sweetness was good.
However, the steamed abalone's internal organs sauce was too salty, so the taste of the abalone was buried, and only the abalone internal sauce remained in the mouth.

Hanchi, which made the first line of the sushi section, was the only one worthy of being called “today’s No. 1 sushi.”
It was cut just enough so that it was soft and sweet.
The sweet shrimp next to it were small and slightly fishy, ​​and the tuna and sea bream were barely memorable.
Then, the sudden reappearance of flounder, amberjack topped with garlic, and the main course, where the tendons kept chewing, gave the impression that the course route was distorted.

The grilled mero was proof that this restaurant ‘knows how to cook.’
The skin is crispy, the flesh is moist, and the burnt taste is minimized to preserve the flavor.
However, the uni rice bowl that came out right away was said to be from Gangwon-do and had a strong bitter taste, and the uni seaweed roll that followed was completely covered in the taste of uni because of the tough seaweed.

I thought the sushi course was over, but freshwater eel rice bowl appeared out of nowhere—fortunately, the ‘main joy’ of the day was this eel.
The seasoning wasn't too much and the meat was soft.
However, Anago sushi followed soon after, making the composition even more confusing.

The Onsoba that came out at the end had soggy noodles and a bland and greasy broth that made people wonder, “Do I really have to eat carbohydrates?” The level I want to be at.
Negidoro was added out of nowhere, and the final blueberry ice cream was a dessert that could have been passed because it had a strong taste of commercially available frozen berries.

reviews.author: Yeah hehe

reviews.author: Bae Tae-cheon

reviews.author: Jintae Kim
reviews.text: It is located on the 2nd basement level of Jongno Tower. There was a passage leading directly to Exit 3-1 of Jonggak Station, so accessibility was good. reviews.author: Simon Shim
reviews.text: As Tanghwa Kung Fu Maratang is a chain restaurant, the taste is strange. You can think of ordering as almost everything being self-administered through the table ordering system. It is a system where you put the vegetables and ingredients you want to eat by yourself, pay the price by weight and start cooking, and when the vibrating bell rings, you can take it and eat it. It may be a bit difficult for older people to use it. However, it seemed like they didn't clean the table themselves and it didn't seem like the table was cleaned right away. Anyway, I recommend it if you are looking for mara xianggu or malatang that never fails.

reviews.author: Marcia Lima
reviews.text:
It is no exaggeration to say that it is one of the best Malatang restaurants in the area. ✨ Perfect for eating alone ✨

When you enter the store, you can pick up a bowl and select the ingredients you want, such as vegetables, noodles, meat, and mushrooms. When you weigh it and tell it how spicy you want it to be, it gives you a vibrating bell and cooks it right away.

Even though I chose a lot of ingredients, it only cost 10,000 won, so the price is not burdensome.

Rice, various sauces, and water are also provided for free. The inside of the store was spacious and clean, which was nice. I will definitely come back soon 🥰😋

reviews.author: EJ N.
reviews.text: I add aged kimchi to buckwheat pancakes, and the two go together really well. I enjoyed it. reviews.author: Gamma Kim

I wasn't able to take a few pictures because I was hungry and anxious.

reviews.author: Jiwon Yoon

Still, there was no cucumber flavor, and the buckwheat flavor was strong as soon as I took my first bite. It was delicious.

reviews.text:
I visited because I heard that Jjajang was delicious.
It feels stuffy and uncomfortable because too many tables are placed in a moderately large space.

reviews.author: E-projectNeudot Project
reviews.text:
Oh.. I really really liked the taste haha.
The rating is lower than I thought(?)

First of all, you can really eat Chinese-style shabu-shabu that Chinese people make!
It tastes different from malatang!! If you like Chinese-style shabu-shabu, or if you like overseas Southeast Asian food, beef soup noodles, or things with a bit of flavor, you will 100% like it ^^ I heard it is run by a famous Chinese chef.. It's delicious!!

It has a simple yet Chinese taste... I don't know how to explain it. I had the Huangshan Shabu beef set without seafood, and the portion was really generous. They gave it to me as a service, but even though it was a service, it was a lot. Very good~~!!!

The white soup and red soup were so delicious that I actually want to go again... but I'm worried because it's not easy to get to Unseo Station from Seoul ^^;;

Sure, Koreans can be a bit frustrated...
It wasn't that uncomfortable.

reviews.text:

Dinner is 20,000 won per person for basic shabu-shabu (without seafood), but lunch is 12,000 won, so lunch is the best value for money.

reviews.author: Kevin Ko
reviews.text: This is a traditional Chinese shabu-shabu hotpot restaurant located on the first basement level of Doosan We've Pavilion near Jongno-gu Office. You can choose between beef and lamb. You can eat red and white soup in a Taegeuk pot by adding vegetables, mushrooms, bean sprouts, meat, etc. to your taste, and the portions are generous and delicious. It also includes kkoopo rou.

reviews.author: jay Kim
reviews.text: There were no customers even though it was dinner time, perhaps due to the Corona 2.5 level social distancing. Although it is run by a Korean, they are friendly and understand Korean well. I ordered lamb and beef for 20,000 won per person. The hotpot dish with alternating white and red soup was delicious. reviews.author: Jong-gyu Lee

reviews.author: PintGlass Yellow
reviews.text:
The taste of the broth is a little different from the one I tried in Taiwan, but the deep and clean taste of beef that Koreans are familiar with. To put it simply, it tastes like a thick Australian-style pho beef broth. The contents of the beef noodles are very substantial (the beef noodles are rich) and the texture of the noodles is also very good.
The side menu, Sugyo, is clean and light with the flavors of meat and shrimp blending well together.
Cucumber salad goes so well with beef noodles that it is considered essential.
It feels like the thick broth that can easily bite you is washed away with just a piece of cucumber salad.
Waiting times are standard, so if possible, we recommend visiting about an hour before normal meal times.

reviews.author: black and white
reviews.text:
Located near Jonggak Station, Jongno-gu
I went to Beef Myeongwan Gwanghwamun branch.

This restaurant is also featured in the Michelin Guide.
I was worried there would be a wait, but it took a long time.
There was no waiting

The signature menu here is beef noodle soup.
Sugyo fish scented eggplant cucumber salad
I ordered a variety of dishes and tried them.

The first beef noodle soup I tried was brisket and gin.
Arongsaeopjinsal is rich in soup
The taste is deep and rich, but not greasy.
The clean aftertaste was excellent.

The sugyo we ordered together was wrapped in a chewy dumpling skin.
It's full of gravy, so when you take a bite,
The savory flavor spread throughout my mouth.

Fish-flavored eggplants that can only be tasted in the evening
Crispy fried eggplant with sweet and spicy sauce
It was well-soaked and was perfect as a side dish for drinks.

The sour cucumber salad is a treat every now and then.
It was a perfect combination to go with it.

Here are some tips to enjoy beef noodles more deliciously:
At first, I enjoyed the original taste of the soup, and then at the table.
Add the spicy soy sauce and make it spicy.
I recommend enjoying it.

Lastly, add rice to the remaining broth and top it with mustard kimchi.
You can enjoy a more satisfying meal if you eat them together.

reviews.text:

I want to visit again next time

reviews.author: taewon Park
reviews.text:
The moment you take your first spoonful of Jinjung Beef Myeonggwan’s beef noodle soup, you will be impressed by its deep, rich flavor.

The red-colored soup is spicy but not greasy and clean.

The broth, made with an appropriate mix of red pepper powder and spices, tastes cool and refreshing the more you chew it, and warms you to the core.

The spicy yet deep umami flavor is attractive.

The tender beef topped with plenty of broth melts the moment you put it in your mouth.

Even though it has been boiled for a long time, the texture is still intact, it has a great chew, and it retains the taste of the broth. The chewy noodles go well with the soup and create a perfect harmony.

reviews.author: H K
reviews.text:
Really objective review along the way..
First impression was, wow! A real Vietnamese local pho restaurant!
It's nice that the interior recreates the atmosphere of a restaurant you'd find on a street corner in Vietnam... but it even recreates the inconveniences...
(A tissue case that doesn't pull out well and ends up blowing away toilet paper powder. Condiment containers and menu boards that are messy and unorganized, etc.)
If the taste, which is the essence of the rest of the restaurant, was properly supported by local taste, it would have had a strong local feel...
The taste is ambiguous. We had nem (4 pieces), pork fried rice, morning glory, bun cha... and it seemed like it wasn't enough, so we ordered the basic puff... 1 epi, 3 main dishes and 1 side dish.
Nem is good because it has a local scent.. 4 for the price.. hmm..
That's right... the portion size isn't that much compared to the price and the overall restaurant environment...
The fried rice and buncha meat is grilled without any fire, but they don't cut it and just give it to you, along with scissors and tongs.
The taste of the meat is not bad... I don't know what the problem is, but it's lacking something by 2%...
Morning Glory is a taste that is commonly eaten locally, but as a person who likes Morning Glory so much, it is a bit inferior.
I was very disappointed because the amount of bun cha was really small. Full of vegetables.. and not enough somen..
To be honest, I was a little disappointed with the most basic Furbo. The key is because of the flavor of the broth.. You shouldn't think of it as a local restaurant where you are drawn by the flavor of the broth while walking down the street.
It's a shame that the red pepper paste isn't too spicy...

Considering that it is located in Jongno, it may be acceptable, but it is not very cost-effective.
If you intuitively expect local food to come at the right time (assuming you know the local taste well), you will be a bit disappointed.
It would have been nice if they had used local food and brought local food, even the inconveniences, and brought the taste.

reviews.author: Majimata
reviews.text:
This is a restaurant where you can enjoy the authentic taste of India, run by an Indian. An Indian fluent in Korean is in charge of serving customers, so there is no difficulty in ordering or paying.

The inside of the store is a fun interior with various textures and objects reminiscent of India, and the vague Indian song playing in the store creates a unique atmosphere.

The curry is full of rich spices and has just the right amount of ingredients and consistency, making it so good that you can just eat it without dipping it in rice or naan.
In the case of naan, there are four types: honey, butter, cheese, and garlic, and the Indian yogurt drink Lassi is available in four types: plain, mango, strawberry, and blueberry. It has a sweet taste, so you can drink it without burden. (Jjai is also sold)
The quality of all the food is excellent, so no matter what you eat, you are guaranteed to enjoy it as long as you do not have any aversion to the unique spicy taste of India.

Recommended as a restaurant where you can enjoy traditional Indian cuisine that is hard to find at a good price and is friendly and highly satisfying.

p.s. As a result of my first visit after a long time, everything else remained the same, but I was disappointed that the capacity of the lassi drink was greatly reduced.

reviews.author: Doctor Tsk Tsk
reviews.text: The owner was friendly and the food was delicious. If you like Thai food, I think you'll be satisfied. The curry was the most delicious I've ever had. The crab didn't get hard on my mouth and went really well with rice. But the most delicious food was the pad thai. The pad thai here is really delicious, so make sure to try it. It's full of flavor. It's hard to rate it because it's my first time eating som tam, but it was sour and delicious. Like lemon juice? The rice noodles had an exotic scent, but the taste was light and refreshing, so it was very delicious🤤 Unfortunately, the unique spice scent of the pad seed oil didn't go well with it. However, it was tasty, and the unique flavor was that of oyster sauce, so it wasn't the most exotic, but I felt like the slight spice scent made it exotic. Also, if you see the review of the owner, can you give me some information about the spoon? I really liked the spoon, so I searched for it, but I couldn't find anything similar.🥲 Anyway, if I go to Seoul again, it's not the most exotic, but the slight spice scent makes it more exotic. I will visit again to try pad thai and foot pad pong curry.

I was unfamiliar with the names of Thai foods, so I asked the owner, and he was very kind and explained things so well that I really wanted to try the whole menu! First of all, be sure to try Pu Pat Pong Curry and Tot Man Goong? (Fried Shrimp Meat)!!! It was really so delicious..!! I ordered Morning Glory or Somtam as a side and kept eating them together, so I didn't get bitten and it was so good🥹

reviews.author: HyoungSeok Lee
reviews.text:
Gappel Kölsch beer was really delicious. Elegant, gorgeous and rich in flavor

The hall was narrower than I thought. And it was Saturday lunch, and we were the only customers from the time we came in until we left. Is it because of Corona???
So I was a little worried about the food, but it turned out to be completely unfounded.
I ordered 500g of Elbone Steak, Puttanesca Pasta, and Tiramisu. Advance reservations are required for T-bone and El-bone. The steak was cooked really gently and the smoky flavor from the fat was really attractive. The round French fries and pickled celery that came together are not often found, but the texture of the French fries was a treat.
The puttanesca pasta was also delicious. The cooked noodles were a bit hard, which was my preference.
Overall, the atmosphere was nice and the taste was very good. There are many people who intend to visit again.

The welcome food may have had some seafood in it, but it didn't go well with the Gappelkölsch beer, so I got a fishy smell when I drank the beer.

reviews.author: Chanho Andrew Kim (MUYO)
reviews.text:
The name of the restaurant was Bistro Kiln because the steaks were grilled in a charcoal kiln. I like dry-aged steak, so I ordered the salchisal steak without much expectation, but the charcoal-flavored, juicy steak, wasabi and mustard sauce, fried egg potatoes, and cream spinach went so well together that it completely changed my opinion of how crispy steak was the best.
The puttanesca pasta we ordered together had an oil base with anchovies and bacon, so it went well with the strong umami and the subtle scent of arugula, and it was well absorbed into the appropriately chewy noodles, making it delicious to the last. In terms of using charcoal, it has a similar concept to "Soot" in Cheongdam, but while "Soot" has a menu that goes all-in on charcoal, Gama is highly regarded for its appropriately used menu and excellent taste for an affordable price.
When things get better, I would like to come back to enjoy an evening with friends and wine.

reviews.author: Kyung Min Kim
reviews.text: The noodles are boiled well to give them the best texture, and I really feel like they are made with fresh, good ingredients. The taste balance is good, you can feel the sincerity and thought put into it, and it's truly Italian. Highly recommended. The owner also kindly explained the food. I think the puttanesca, carbonara, and salchisal steak were especially delicious. It's much better than the steaks I paid twice as much for in Gangnam. It's really... T-bone steak is worth the price, and I highly recommend it for beginners. It's amazing how they grill such thick meat so soft and tender. It must be thanks to the wonderful charcoal kiln, right? For my taste, it would have been better if the sear had been more sizzling, but this is not a place where searing is done too hard. Thanks to this, it has a soft texture. Pucanesca pasta has a fresh, delicious taste that you won't get tired of, so you'll want to eat it again as soon as you get home. Among the Italian carbonaras I've tasted at restaurants, the carbonara followed the basics the best and was the most delicious. The pepper really kills it. The ragu sauce was simple yet very flavorful. I highly recommend the cottage cheese salad. The taste of prosciutto and homemade chewy cheese is truly intoxicating. I highly recommend it as a starter. The store has a pretty wooden interior. I recommend it for anniversaries, but it would also be great for meeting friends or with family. Since the store is not large, it would be a good idea to make a reservation. It's so delicious that I think I'll eat it alone.
